subject.title: feat(workboard): add durable status_changed notification event

question: Should Workboard expose `status_changed` as a durable subscriber contract requiring independently retained transition records, or should this proposal be narrowed to a clearly non-durable/read-time convenience signal?
rationale: The requested capability creates a new cross-consumer contract; choosing its retention, replay, and scope guarantees determines the appropriate data model and cannot be settled by a local patch alone.

options.title: Ship a truly durable contract
options.body: Persist immutable transition records with the status-change scope captured at update time, then retain the opt-in notification API.

options.title: Narrow the capability
options.body: Keep a read-time signal only if the API and documentation explicitly exclude durable replay and historical completeness.

options.title: Defer the producer API
options.body: Close or pause this implementation until a downstream consumer and owner confirm the required replay semantics.

recommendation.title: Ship a truly durable contract
recommendation.body: Persist immutable transition records with the status-change scope captured at update time, then retain the opt-in notification API.

likelyOwner.reason: No current-main Workboard ownership provenance was available in the supplied review evidence.
